ex: Ginseng water as the first step, in place of a plain toner.
d: Ginseng is the backbone of hanbang skincare, and using it as the water in the formula rather than an added extract is what makes this essence worth the step.
Thin, slightly amber, and it sinks in before you have finished pressing it on.
bn: Preps skin to take the next steps

ex: A resurfacing toner with kojic acid, for marks and rough texture.
d: Gentle PHA exfoliation clears the way and kojic acid gets to work on pigment, which is how a toner ends up doing more than wiping.
The first step of Medicube's dark spot routine.
bn: Preps skin for the serum that follows
caution: Contains exfoliating acids. Wear sunscreen daily.

ex: Fermented black rice, with no alcohol and no fragrance anywhere.
d: haruharu wonder ferment Korean black rice and use it instead of water, then leave out everything sensitive skin usually reacts to.
It is the toner people switch to when every other toner has stung.

n: Madagascar Centella Tone Brightening Boosting Toner
ex: The brightening toner of the centella range.
d: A first step that starts the tone work rather than just wetting the skin, with centella keeping it gentle enough for daily use.
Pairs with the matching ampoule and cream.
bn: Begins brightening at the first step

ex: A probiotic essence built on makgeolli - fermented rice wine.
d: The probiotic ferment is what makgeolli brewers have used for centuries, repurposed here to feed the skin's own microbiome.
Milky and light, and it goes on after the toner rather than instead of it.
bn: Milky texture that sinks straight in

ex: Soaked pads that exfoliate and brighten in one wipe.
d: The pad does the physical work and the kojic acid does the chemical work, which together clear the dull top layer that makes marks look worse.
Sixty pads, so it lasts a proper course.
bn: Brightens and exfoliates in one step
No cotton pad or decanting needed
caution: Start every other night. Wear sunscreen daily.

ex: Gentle PHA pads in Anua's heartleaf base.
d: PHA is the largest of the exfoliating acids, so it works on the surface and stays out of the deeper layers that react.
77% heartleaf in the liquid means the calming and the exfoliating happen together.

ex: 80% green tea, for oily skin that needs a reset.
d: Green tea is the plant answer to shine, and Isntree use it as the base of the formula rather than a line on the label.
A touch of BHA keeps pores from filling back up.

ex: Azelaic acid in a toner, for skin that breaks out constantly.
d: Getting azelaic acid into the first step means it is on the skin for the whole routine rather than in one thin layer.
Good for the bumpy, red, congested kind of breakout rather than the occasional spot.
caution: Introduce gradually and wear sunscreen daily.

n: Seoul 1988 Time Shift Toner - Snail Mucin 97% + Rice
ex: 97% snail mucin in a pump toner, with rice for tone.
d: At 97% the mucin is essentially the product, which is the concentration you want if you are using it for repair rather than slip.
Rice extract handles the brightening side.
bn: Repairs and plumps with 97% snail mucin
Softens the look of fine lines

ex: The hydrating-and-brightening toner in the blue line.
d: Hyaluronic acid pulls the water in, centella keeps the skin calm, niacinamide handles the tone - a first step that covers three jobs.
Thin enough to use in several layers on a dry day.
bn: Hydrates deeply at the first step

n: AHA BHA PHA 30 Days Miracle Toner
ex: The toner behind the 30-day challenge everyone posted about.
d: Three acids at once, which is why the 30-day framing exists: it is a course, not a forever product.
Tea tree sits underneath to keep breakouts from coming straight back.
bn: Tea tree keeps skin clear after
caution: Use at night, starting every other day. Sunscreen is essential.

ex: 77% rice extract - the cult toner for dull, dry skin.
d: Thicker than most toners, closer to an essence, and it is the product that put I'm From on every shelf.
Rice brightens slowly and hydrates immediately, which is a good combination to start a routine with.

ex: A milky rice toner with ceramides folded in.
d: Milky toners suit dry skin better than watery ones, and the ceramides mean this one repairs rather than just wets.
Anua's answer for skin that is dull because it is dehydrated.

ex: The toner that starts Medicube's collagen routine.
d: Collagen in the first step gets it onto bare skin, where it has the best chance of being taken up.
Light and slightly milky, so it works under the matching serum and cream.
bn: Pairs with the collagen serum and cream

ex: A probiotic centella essence for an unsettled microbiome.
d: Skin that breaks out and reacts at the same time usually has a microbiome problem, which is what the probiotic ferment is for.
Centella handles the visible redness while that settles.

ex: PDRN repair with oat water, in a toner gentle enough for daily use.
d: Refining usually means acid; here it means PDRN and oat, which get to smoother skin without the sting.
A good choice if your skin cannot tolerate an exfoliating toner but needs one.
bn: Oat water calms as it works

ex: The everyday centella toner, for tone and balance.
d: The plain one in the range, and the one most people end up buying repeatedly.
Balances oil, evens out tone, and gets the next step absorbing properly.
bn: Good value in a large bottle

ex: A big bottle of moisture-exfoliating toner, named for how much of it there is.
d: 400ml, so you can use it with a cotton pad every morning without counting.
Gentle PHA keeps the skin smooth while the hyaluronic acid holds the water in.
bn: Good for body use as well as face

ex: Exosome technology in the calming toner of the range.
d: Exosomes are the signalling ingredient Korean clinics moved into home care, and here they sit alongside centella, heartleaf and tea tree.
Aimed at skin that is irritated and breaking out at once.

ex: The hydrating version of Anua's famous heartleaf toner.
d: The original heartleaf toner calms; this one calms and holds water, which is what skin needs when it is both reactive and dehydrated.
250ml, and most people use it in several layers.
bn: Holds hydration at the first step
Layers well, several at a time

ex: Tea tree and centella, for congested, oily skin.
d: The purifying member of the centella family: tea tree and a little salicylic acid for pores, centella so your skin does not pay for it.
The toner for the oily, blemish-prone end of the range.
caution: Contains salicylic acid. Wear sunscreen daily.

ex: Vitamin C pads, for brightening without a separate bottle.
d: A soaked pad is an easy way to get vitamin C onto the whole face evenly, and the wipe takes the dull top layer with it.
70 pads, which is roughly a two-month course.

ex: Niacinamide and tranexamic acid pads, for marks that linger.
d: The two best-evidenced pigment ingredients short of prescription, delivered on a pad so they go on evenly.
60 pads, used at night after cleansing.
caution: Use sunscreen daily, or the marks come back.

n: Azelaic Acid 10 + Hyaluron Redness Soothing Pad
ex: 10% azelaic acid pads, aimed at redness and bumps.
d: Azelaic acid is the ingredient for skin that is red, bumpy and breaking out at once, and a pad is the easiest way to cover the whole face with it.
Hyaluronic acid keeps the dryness that normally follows at bay.
bn: 10% azelaic acid in an easy format
Hydrates so skin does not dry out

ex: The pore pads that made Medicube a household name.
d: AHA on the surface and BHA down in the pore, on a textured pad that does some of the lifting itself.
The single product most people buy from Medicube first.
bn: Controls oil for the rest of the day
caution: Contains AHA and BHA. Start every other night and wear sunscreen daily.

ex: The brightening number of the range, in pad form.
d: Same brightening set as the No.5 serum, on a pad for the nights when you want the step to take ten seconds.
The embossed side lifts dull surface skin as you wipe.
